clue.text: Polish army corps rise for the last daily exam

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: the last signals taking only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: its final letter is Y
an exam is a paper

explanation.surface: A soldier from an army corps is told to stand up for the final exam of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's corps of engineers; it rises (reads upwards in this down entry) as EMER, then Y from the end of 'daily' and PAPER for the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery paper is an abrasive sheet used for polishing or smoothing metal, so it is something that polishes.

clue.text: Charge for languages group on Tuesday

parts.note: Indic is the group of Indo-Aryan languages of India

explanation.surface: A fee being levied on a language school's class held on Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict someone is to formally accuse them of a crime, i.e. to charge them in law.

clue.text: More vino ordered for one who'll eat anything

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new arrangement, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who orders more wine at dinner is happy to eat whatever comes.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore is a creature whose diet takes in both plants and meat, so it eats virtually any food.

clue.text: It bites; bite back

indicators.note: back means the letters are taken in the opposite direction

parts.note: bite as in a sharp flavour, which is tang

explanation.surface: Something bites you, so you bite it in return.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'bite' is a noun meaning sharpness of taste, TANG, which turned back gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small fly whose females pierce skin to feed, an insect that bites people.

clue.text: Peak concern as Spike loses time

parts.note: a concern is a matter, an issue

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a spike is a thorn

explanation.surface: A worry arises when someone called Spike runs out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: THORN loses its T to give HORN, appended to MATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Matterhorn is a famous Alpine mountain on the Swiss-Italian border, a celebrated summit.

clue.text: Not least, schoolmates regrouped for slow dance

indicators.note: Not says the letters of the following word are to be left out of the mix
regrouped means the remaining letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: these letters are the ones subtracted from the fodder

explanation.surface: Classmates gather again at a reunion for a slow dance, all but the smallest of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of LEAST out of SCHOOLMATES and rearrange the six that remain: S, C, H, O, O, M.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooch is to dance slowly in a close embrace, the cheek-to-cheek shuffle at the end of a party.

clue.text: Sweater one considered, so to speak

indicators.note: considered can mean thought over and reworked, here signalling that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about a sweater, as you might say.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a figurative hedge used to soften an expression, meaning in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Bond problem for host

parts.note: a host is a great multitude; K stands for a thousand, a large number
a nit, a louse egg, is a problem for whoever hosts it

explanation.surface: A tie or connection creates difficulties for whoever is hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a single problem for a host; it splits as K for the host (a thousand) and NIT, a louse egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to join closely together, as broken bones knit, so it means to bond or unite.

clue.text: He's great when it comes to knocking things into shape!

definitions.text: He's great when it comes to knocking things into shape!

parts.words: He's great when it comes to knocking things into shape!
parts.note: monumental can mean great, and the person who chisels stone into shape is a mason, so the whole clue describes a gravestone carver

explanation.surface: Praise for a personal trainer or fixer who sorts anything out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' reads as praise, but it is the first word of the answer, and 'knocking into shape' is literal chiselling of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A monumental mason carves headstones and memorials, hammering stone blocks into finished forms.

clue.text: Handy therapy for first responders; evidently it's kicking in

indicators.note: first tells us to take the opening letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hands-on treatment recommended for paramedics, apparently starting to take effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First responders' looks like a phrase about paramedics, but 'first' applies to responders and the four words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiki is a healing practice in which the practitioner places hands on or over the body, hence a therapy done by hand.

clue.text: Retribution for Cockney's hat, said tasteless thing

indicators.note: said means the slang word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: titfer is Cockney slang for a hat
tat is cheap, tasteless stuff

explanation.surface: Payback for a Londoner's cap that was called a piece of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners; their rhyming slang for hat is tit-for-tat, shortened to titfer, which said aloud gives the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is the giving of like for like in return for an injury, i.e. retaliation.

clue.text: Girl, 10, finds exit that could lead to deck

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the thing that leads out to a deck

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
the number 10 is written with the digits 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O
a door is a way out

explanation.surface: A girl of ten discovers a way out onto the terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures 1 and 0 in 10 look like the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio door is a glazed sliding door opening onto a patio or wooden decking outside the house.

clue.text: Has more books around 2nd June, and the 4th in particular

indicators.note: around means the books' abbreviation wraps round the next letter

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

indicators.note: 2nd says to take the second letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its second letter is U
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone owns more books by early June, the fourth in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 4th in particular' looks like more letter-picking, but it names a whole book: the fourth book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber is to be greater in count than another group, to have a larger quantity.

clue.text: Animal hunger in central Sahara

indicators.note: in means this word is placed inside the other letters
central means take the middle letters of the word that follows

parts.note: its two middle letters are HA
a yen is a longing or hunger

explanation.surface: A beast goes hungry in the heart of the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: A word of even length has two central letters, so 'central' takes a pair here.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a carnivorous African mammal, a scavenging beast known for its laugh-like call.

clue.text: Out St Basil, revealed as having totalitarian views

indicators.note: revealed here means turned out in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint is exposed as harbouring dictatorial opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like part of the exposé, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolutist supports absolute rule by an unrestricted authority, the political stance of authoritarian regimes.

clue.text: Pensions trustee charged with arrogance

indicators.note: charged in the sense of excited or shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The person running a pension fund is prosecuted for being high-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentiousness is a showy claim to importance or merit, a kind of self-important conceit.

clue.text: Mules, for your information, made ready to be mixed up

definitions.note: a past-tense phrase standing for the verb, to cause to blend

indicators.note: made ready means prepared or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A memo notes that the mules have been prepared to be blended.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulsify is to combine liquids that do not normally blend, such as oil and water, into a smooth emulsion.

clue.text: Don't move, especially when drunk!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stay where you are and do nothing
second meaning, playful: tight means drunk, so a drunk should sit while tight

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a joke advice: tight is slang for drunk, and the intoxicated are best kept seated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an instruction to stay put and wait, refraining from any action.

clue.text: Ladies' man in final French city…

parts.note: a roué is a dissolute womaniser

indicators.note: final means take only the last letter of the word in

parts.note: its last letter is N

explanation.surface: A womaniser in his last French town, the trail continuing in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is the historic capital of Normandy in northern France, on the Seine.

clue.text: Tell Barry's finally able to be working at levitating!

indicators.note: in a down clue, levitating means the letters rise and so read upwards
finally means take the last letter of Barry's name

parts.note: the last letter of Barry is Y
fit means able, capable
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: Someone tells Barry he's at last managing to float in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, FIT and ON together are YFITON; 'levitating' lifts them, reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify is to inform someone formally, to let them know something.

clue.text: …where one is spontaneous; that's extraordinary

parts.note: un is French for one; 'where' points back to the French city in the previous clue
natural means spontaneous, unaffected

explanation.surface: Continuing the tale: a city where a person is unaffected, which is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to Rouen, so 'where one is' means how one is said there: UN, the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnatural means abnormal or contrary to the ordinary course of things, out of the usual.

clue.text: Stand-in is somewhat more gentlemanly

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deputy is described as rather more courteous than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules on behalf of a monarch who is too young, absent or ill, acting as a substitute.

clue.text: Experimental glassware for analysis by part of London Transport?

parts.note: a test is an analysis
the Tube is London's underground railway; tubes are its trains or lines

explanation.surface: Lab equipment needed to examine the London Underground, with a question mark for the whimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground railway network.
explanation.definitionFit: Test tubes are thin glass cylinders used in laboratories to hold samples during experiments.

clue.text: Work engagement ends with question

indicators.note: ends points to the final letter of engagement

parts.note: its last letter is T
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: A job booking finishes with a query.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work assigned to someone, a job to be done.

clue.text: Almost broke cover

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, having no money

explanation.surface: Nearly out of money, someone shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin is the outer layer that covers a body or fruit, a natural covering.

clue.text: Searching Ottawa to find a bar

indicators.note: to find tells us to discover the answer sitting inside the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone combs the Canadian capital looking for a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a drinking place, but it is a block of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, usually gold or silver, shaped like a brick.

clue.text: Fluffy Finnish rugs made for decorating the home

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for things used in decorating the home

parts.note: fluffy things are soft

indicators.note: made here means made up into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plush Scandinavian rugs produced to adorn a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft furnishings are curtains, cushions and rugs: fabric items that furnish and decorate a room.
